international.title: Wages grow at fastest pace since 2023 – but prices are climbing even more quickly
international.summary: Wage rates climb about 1 percentage point faster than before pandemic, triggering warnings of a sixth RBA rate rise Wages grew at their fastest pace since late 2023 over the three months to September, buoyed by this year’s boost to minimum pay rates for millions of lower paid workers – but still not fast enough to keep up with the rising cost of living. The Australian Bureau of Statistics’ wage price index climbed by 1.1% in the most recent quarter, lifting the annual increase to 3.5% – a pace that economists said would keep the Reserve Bank on edge about the need for further interest rate hikes.
